claim: Consider two equally weighted biallelic populations whose exact allele-A frequencies are \(a/m\) and \(b/m\), with \(1\le a,b\le m-1\), so both alleles are present in both populations. Let \(G_{ST}=(H_T-H_S)/H_T\) and let Jost differentiation be \(D=2(H_T-H_S)/(1-H_S)\). Put \(d=|a-b|\) and \(t=|a+b-m|\). Then \(G_{ST}=d^2/(m^2-t^2)\) and \(D=2d^2/(m^2+d^2+t^2)\). Consequently, among population pairs with the same nonzero allele-count gap \(d\), moving the pooled allele frequency farther from one half strictly increases \(G_{ST}\) but strictly decreases Jost \(D\). For denominator \(m\le4\), no two polymorphic biallelic population pairs receive opposite strict rankings from \(G_{ST}\) and \(D\). Denominator \(m=5\) is sharp: up to exchanging the two populations and globally relabeling the two alleles, the unique first reversal compares count pairs \((1,2)\) and \((2,3)\). The first has \(G_{ST}=1/21>1/25\) but \(D=1/15<1/13\). Moreover, strict reversal persists for every \(m\ge5\): compare \((1,2)\) with the adjacent central pair \(((m-1)/2,(m+1)/2)\) when \(m\) is odd, or with \((m/2-1,m/2)\) when \(m\) is even.
integrity: The algebraic reduction is exact: with allele-count gap d and pooled imbalance t, GST=d^2/(m^2-t^2) and Jost D=2d^2/(m^2+d^2+t^2). The packaged verifier exhaustively checks the complete positive grids through the sharp denominator and replays the structural family with exact rational arithmetic.
scientific_limitations: One biallelic locus, two equally weighted populations, exact rational frequencies on a common denominator, and both alleles present in both populations. The theorem uses theoretical heterozygosity quantities rather than finite-sample bias-corrected estimators; allowing fixation gives smaller-grid reversals.
title: Five copies per population are the sharp polymorphic biallelic G_ST–Jost D ranking-reversal boundary
